answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity, including services named ember, nectar and delta, to lock 100 units of a scarce collateral asset for 30 days before it can bid for work. The registry holds a separate bond for each identity, so the same funds cannot back multiple accounts at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 units for a month, making a swarm costly even when generating keys is free.
